chunks: Al-Tawhid: My father, from Sa'd, from Ibn Abi al-Khattab, from al-Bazanti who said:

A group came from Beyond the River to Abi al-Hasan (peace be upon him) and said to him: We have come to ask you three questions. If you answer us in them we will know that you are the Scholar. He said: Ask. They said: Inform us about Allah - Where was He? How was He? Upon what thing was His reliance? He said: Allah Mighty and Majestic howed the how so he is without ‘how’ and whered the where so He is without ‘where’ and His reliance was on His Power. They said: We bear witness that you are the Scholar.
ai.seo_question: What are the three questions asked to Imam al-Hassan regarding God's attributes of place and manner?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights the Shia doctrine of divine transcendence (tanzih), where Imam al-Hassan al-Ridha (AS) refutes anthropomorphic conceptions by asserting that God is beyond spatial dimensions ('where') and qualitative modes ('how'). The Imam identifies God's reliance not on an external support but on His own infinite Power (Qudrah), a concept deeply rooted in the Mu'tazili and Shia theological emphasis on divine unity and independence. The interlocutors' immediate acknowledgment of his wisdom underscores the Imam's role as the definitive interpreter of metaphysical truths.
